findings: The body is clamped; its spin angular momentum is explicitly minus magnetic moment divided by positive gamma. Gilbert damping deposits angular momentum locally into the measured body, and other sinks are excluded. Body-on-support torque has a unique sign.

With fixed body orientation, angular momentum balance gives body-on-support torque equal to applied magnetic torque minus spin angular-momentum rate. Substitution of the stated Gilbert equation gives alpha times moment/gamma times m cross dm/dt.

The starter exactly solves the positive near-aligned finite-drive periodic Gilbert state. Its stable quadratic root, phase rotation and applied magnetic torque are mathematically correct; its only physical error is attributing that applied torque entirely to the support.

The z spin component is constant in this periodic state, so applied and mechanical z torques coincide at every phase. This provides informative nonzero calibration for moment while transverse signals retain a spin-storage contribution.

The oracle evaluates the local Gilbert torque; the independent reference integrates nonlinear laboratory-frame dynamics from the prescribed initial state and obtains support torque from external torque minus spin rate. It does not reuse the quadratic rotating-frame solution.
Public preparation, sensor sign and locality of the damping channel fix the experiment without giving the torque-balance correction, prescribing a solver or restricting edits.
